images.title: Newspapers collected in a week
images.purpose: Show the bar graph of the newspapers a class collects on five days, so the student can find the highest and the lowest bar and add the bars for a total of 20 kg.
images.composition: One bar graph titled Newspapers (kg): the vertical line marked 0 to 7 and the horizontal base with Monday to Friday, with five amber bars of 3, 6, 4, 5 and 2.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, one bar graph. The title Newspapers (kg) is centred at (728, 70) in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (48 px). a vertical line (dark #2B2B2B, 4 px) at x 260 from y 650 up to y 150, with exactly 8 marks: a short tick (14 px) to the left of the line at every whole number from 0 to 7 (0 at y 650 and one mark every 70 px up, so 7 is at y 160), each mark numbered 0 to 7 at its left (right-aligned to x 230, dark #1F2937 bold, 32 px); a horizontal base line (dark #2B2B2B, 4 px) at y 650 from x 260 to x 1330. Exactly 5 bars, all 130 px wide, filled amber #E69F00 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), standing on the base: Monday: x 345 to 475, y 440 to 650 (height 210 px, which is 3 on the vertical line); Tuesday: x 545 to 675, y 230 to 650 (height 420 px, which is 6 on the vertical line); Wednesday: x 745 to 875, y 370 to 650 (height 280 px, which is 4 on the vertical line); Thursday: x 945 to 1075, y 300 to 650 (height 350 px, which is 5 on the vertical line); Friday: x 1145 to 1275, y 510 to 650 (height 140 px, which is 2 on the vertical line). Under the base, centred under each bar, its name in dark #1F2937 (34 px, first line at y 695). No number is written on a bar, and no word such as Number of Hours or Activities, no total and no bag count is written anywhere. In all there are 5 bars and 8 marks on the vertical line. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a bar whose height differs from 3, 6, 4, 5 and 2, or bars of unequal width
a total, a bag count, a bar label or any other number written in the frame
any highlight or arrow on the highest or the lowest bar
images.takeaway: The tallest bar (Tuesday) is the highest and the shortest bar (Friday) is the lowest, and adding all the bars gives the total of 20 kg.
images.description: A bar graph titled Newspapers (kg) with the vertical line marked 0 to 7 and bars Monday 3, Tuesday 6, Wednesday 4, Thursday 5 and Friday 2.
images.context: Concept image for Using a Bar Graph: Totals and Predictions. It follows the idea of the book's bar graph of food wasted on five weekdays and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: newspapers of 3, 6, 4, 5 and 2 kg.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student find the highest and the lowest bar by looking, read each bar, and add them for the total before any rule is used. The slip to watch: adding the days that have the tallest bars only.

image_decisions.why: A bar graph of five days lets the student find the highest and the lowest bar and add the bars for a total before a rule is used.
